\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مہلت} (mohlat)}{مہلت (mohlat)}]{\ur{مہلت} (mohlat) — extra time; a respite}

\label{lesson:UR-C525-mohlat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a way out, then the Urdu for to have (something) made or built.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مہلت}}
\textbf{\ur{مہلت}} — \emph{mohlat} — \textquotedblleft{}extra time; a respite\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{ایک} \ur{ہفتے} \ur{کی} \ur{مہلت} \ur{ملی} \ur{تو} \ur{کام} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar ek hafte kī mohlat milī to kām ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If I get a week's grace, the work will be finished.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مہلت}} (\emph{mohlat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muhla}, \textquotedblleft{}a delay, a respite\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mohlat}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mohlat}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar ek hafte kī mohlat milī to kām ho gā.} — If I get a week's grace, the work will be finished.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a way out, then the Urdu for to have (something) made or built, then say \emph{mohlat} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{مہلت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Extra time; a respite\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{التوا} (iltivā)}{التوا (iltivā)}]{\ur{التوا} (iltivā) — a postponement}

\label{lesson:UR-C525-iltiva}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to have (something) made or built, then the Urdu for extra time.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{التوا}}
\textbf{\ur{التوا}} — \emph{iltivā} — \textquotedblleft{}a postponement\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{التوا} \ur{نہیں} \ur{ہوا} \ur{تو} \ur{امتحان} \ur{کل} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar iltivā nahīṅ huā to imtihān kal ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If it is not postponed, the exam will be tomorrow.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{التوا}} (\emph{iltivā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{iltiwāʾ}, \textquotedblleft{}a bending, a turning aside\textquotedblright{}; the sense \textquotedblleft{}putting off\textquotedblright{} came later, and the sources we use do not show how it arose.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iltivā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iltivā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar iltivā nahīṅ huā to imtihān kal ho gā.} — If it is not postponed, the exam will be tomorrow.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to have (something) made or built, then the Urdu for extra time, then say \emph{iltivā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{التوا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A postponement\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{معطل} (muattal)}{معطل (muattal)}]{\ur{معطل} (muattal) — suspended (for now)}

\label{lesson:UR-C525-muattal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for extra time, then the Urdu for a postponement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{معطل}}
\textbf{\ur{معطل}} — \emph{muattal} — \textquotedblleft{}suspended (for now)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{طوفان} \ur{آیا} \ur{تو} \ur{ریل} \ur{گاڑیاں} \ur{معطل} \ur{ہوں} \ur{گی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tūfān āyā to rel gāṛiyāṅ muattal hoṅ gī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If a storm comes, the trains will be suspended.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{معطل}} (\emph{muattal}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{muʿaṭṭal}, \textquotedblleft{}left idle, put out of use\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muattal}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{muattal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tūfān āyā to rel gāṛiyāṅ muattal hoṅ gī.} — If a storm comes, the trains will be suspended.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for extra time, then the Urdu for a postponement, then say \emph{muattal} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{برقرار} (barqarār)}{برقرار (barqarār)}]{\ur{برقرار} (barqarār) — still standing; unchanged}

\label{lesson:UR-C525-barqarar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a postponement, then the Urdu for suspended.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{برقرار}}
\textbf{\ur{برقرار}} — \emph{barqarār} — \textquotedblleft{}still standing; unchanged\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{موسم} \ur{ٹھیک} \ur{رہا} \ur{تو} \ur{پروگرام} \ur{برقرار} \ur{رہے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar mausam ṭhīk rahā to progrām barqarār rahe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the weather stays fine, the plan will stand.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{برقرار}} (\emph{barqarār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{barqarār}, \textquotedblleft{}firm, established\textquotedblright{}, built from \emph{bar}, \textquotedblleft{}on\textquotedblright{}, and Arabic \emph{qarār}, \textquotedblleft{}rest, firmness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barqarār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{barqarār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar mausam ṭhīk rahā to progrām barqarār rahe gā.} — If the weather stays fine, the plan will stand.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a postponement, then the Urdu for suspended, then say \emph{barqarār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اٹکانا} (aṭkānā)}{اٹکانا (aṭkānā)}]{\ur{اٹکانا} (aṭkānā) — to keep (something) pending; to hold up}

\label{lesson:UR-C525-atkana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for suspended, then the Urdu for still standing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اٹکانا}}
\textbf{\ur{اٹکانا}} — \emph{aṭkānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to keep (something) pending; to hold up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{افسر} \ur{نے} \ur{فائل} \ur{اٹکائی} \ur{تو} \ur{کام} \ur{رک} \ur{جائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar afsar ne fāil aṭkāī to kām ruk jāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If the officer holds up the file, the work will stop.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{میری} \ur{فائل} \ur{اٹکائی}, \emph{us ne merī fāil aṭkāī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اٹکانا}} (\emph{aṭkānā}) is the causative of \emph{aṭaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to get stuck\textquotedblright{}, which CDIAL lists under \emph{*aṭṭakk}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 182).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭkānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{aṭkānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar afsar ne fāil aṭkāī to kām ruk jāe gā.} — If the officer holds up the file, the work will stop.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for suspended, then the Urdu for still standing, then say \emph{aṭkānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{اٹکانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To keep (something) pending; to hold up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Learning to Sing to Putting Things Off}

\label{lesson:UR-R525-review-518-525}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for a voice and melodious.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item a voice, melodious, a raga, practice (in music), to hum
  \item a drum, a musical instrument, qawwali, a gathering (for music or poetry), to make (someone) dance
  \item a wrestler, an Indian club (for exercise), a move (in wrestling), to pit against each other, a loincloth
  \item a match (a game), a tournament, a captain (of a team), a winner, a defeat
  \item agility, to bend without breaking, to roll (something) along, to make (someone) run, a trophy
  \item a stadium, an umpire, a score, a cheer, to leap over
  \item a list, a draft, to have (something) printed, a way out, to have (something) made or built
  \item extra time, a postponement, suspended, still standing, to keep (something) pending
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
A voice? (\textbf{\ur{آواز}}, \emph{āvāz}.) Melodious? (\textbf{\ur{سریلا}}, \emph{surīlā}.) A raga? (\textbf{\ur{راگ}}, \emph{rāg}.) Practice (in music)? (\textbf{\ur{ریاض}}, \emph{riyāz}.) To hum? (\textbf{\ur{گنگنانا}}, \emph{gungunānā}.) A drum? (\textbf{\ur{ڈھول}}, \emph{ḍhol}.) A musical instrument? (\textbf{\ur{ساز}}, \emph{sāz}.) Qawwali? (\textbf{\ur{قوالی}}, \emph{qavvālī}.) A gathering (for music or poetry)? (\textbf{\ur{محفل}}, \emph{mahfil}.) To make (someone) dance? (\textbf{\ur{نچانا}}, \emph{nachānā}.) A wrestler? (\textbf{\ur{پہلوان}}, \emph{pahalvān}.) An Indian club (for exercise)? (\textbf{\ur{مگدر}}, \emph{mugdar}.) A move (in wrestling)? (\textbf{\ur{داؤ}}, \emph{dāo}.) To pit against each other? (\textbf{\ur{بھڑانا}}, \emph{bhiṛānā}.) A loincloth? (\textbf{\ur{لنگوٹ}}, \emph{langoṭ}.) A match (a game)? (\textbf{\ur{میچ}}, \emph{maich}.) A tournament? (\textbf{\ur{ٹورنامنٹ}}, \emph{ṭūrnāmenṭ}.) A captain (of a team)? (\textbf{\ur{کپتان}}, \emph{kaptān}.) A winner? (\textbf{\ur{فاتح}}, \emph{fātih}.) A defeat? (\textbf{\ur{شکست}}, \emph{shikast}.) Agility? (\textbf{\ur{پھرتی}}, \emph{phurtī}.) To bend without breaking? (\textbf{\ur{لچکنا}}, \emph{lachaknā}.) To roll (something) along? (\textbf{\ur{لڑھکانا}}, \emph{luṛhkānā}.) To make (someone) run? (\textbf{\ur{دوڑانا}}, \emph{dauṛānā}.) A trophy? (\textbf{\ur{ٹرافی}}, \emph{ṭrāfī}.) A stadium? (\textbf{\ur{اسٹیڈیم}}, \emph{isṭeḍiyam}.) An umpire? (\textbf{\ur{امپائر}}, \emph{ampāyar}.) A score? (\textbf{\ur{اسکور}}, \emph{iskor}.) A cheer? (\textbf{\ur{نعرہ}}, \emph{nārā}.) To leap over? (\textbf{\ur{پھاندنا}}, \emph{phāṅdnā}.) A list? (\textbf{\ur{فہرست}}, \emph{fehrist}.) A draft? (\textbf{\ur{مسودہ}}, \emph{musavvadā}.) To have (something) printed? (\textbf{\ur{چھپوانا}}, \emph{chhapvānā}.) A way out? (\textbf{\ur{تدبیر}}, \emph{tadbīr}.) To have (something) made or built? (\textbf{\ur{بنوانا}}, \emph{banvānā}.) Extra time? (\textbf{\ur{مہلت}}, \emph{mohlat}.) A postponement? (\textbf{\ur{التوا}}, \emph{iltivā}.) Suspended? (\textbf{\ur{معطل}}, \emph{muattal}.) Still standing? (\textbf{\ur{برقرار}}, \emph{barqarār}.) To keep (something) pending? (\textbf{\ur{اٹکانا}}, \emph{aṭkānā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
